name: Ryn Castle
architectural_style: A Teutonic Order castle built around 1377 to replace a smaller stronghold, dismantled after the Order's defeat at Grunwald in 1410, burned by Tatar forces in 1657 and again in 1881, and substantially rebuilt since — the hotel occupies what is largely later reconstruction rather than untouched 14th-century fabric
accessibility: A castle hotel by the town's main square; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: A Teutonic Order commandery built around 1377 for Grand Master Winrich von Kniprode, burned by Tatars in 1657 and again in 1881 — now a lakeside castle hotel on Masuria's Lake Ołów, with knightly feasts and a spa
highlights: Built by the Teutonic Order around 1377 under Grand Master Winrich von Kniprode, replacing a smaller stronghold, as a commandery and base against the Grand Duchy of Lithuania
Fortifications dismantled after the Order's defeat at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410
Burned by Tatar forces in 1657, used as a prison in the 19th century, and burned again in 1881
Served after 1945 as a community centre, small museum and town office before its later conversion into a hotel
Stands between the town of Ryn and Lake Ołów, in the heart of the Masurian Lake District
description:
Ryn Castle stands between the town of Ryn and Lake Ołów, in Poland's Masurian Lake District, built by the Teutonic Order around 1377 under Grand Master Winrich von Kniprode to replace an earlier, smaller stronghold. It served as a commandery and a forward base for the Order's operations against the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, part of the wider network of Teutonic fortifications that once controlled this borderland.

The castle's military role ended abruptly after the Order's defeat at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410, when its fortifications were dismantled. Its later history was no gentler: Tatar forces burned the castle in 1657, during the Second Northern War, and it served as a prison through the 19th century before burning again in 1881. What stands today is largely the product of rebuilding after these fires rather than untouched medieval fabric, even though the castle's silhouette by the town's main square still reads as thoroughly historic.

After 1945, the building passed through a sequence of civic uses — a community centre, a small museum, and the town office — before its eventual conversion into a hotel; sources disagree on the exact year this happened, so no single date is given here. Today it operates as a castle hotel with its own restaurant, Refektarz, serving dishes inspired by Teutonic Knights' cuisine, alongside a spa and knightly feasts held in the courtyard.
history: Ryn Castle was built by the Teutonic Order around 1377 under Grand Master Winrich von Kniprode, replacing a smaller stronghold, to serve as a commandery and a base for operations against the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. After the Order's defeat at Grunwald in 1410 its fortifications were dismantled; the castle was burned by Tatar forces in 1657, used as a prison in the 19th century and burned again in 1881. After 1945 it served as a community centre, small museum and town office, and was later converted into a hotel.

faqs.question: Is Ryn Castle still a 14th-century building inside?
faqs.answer: Mostly not — the castle was burned in 1657 and again in 1881, and what stands today is largely later reconstruction rather than untouched medieval fabric, even though the site has been fortified since around 1377.

faqs.question: When did Ryn Castle become a hotel?
faqs.answer: Sources differ on the exact year the conversion happened, so no single date is given here. The building passed through use as a community centre, small museum and town office after 1945 before its later conversion to a hotel.

meta_title: Ryn Castle, Masuria — Lakeside Castle Hotel in Poland
meta_description: Stay at Ryn Castle on Lake Ołów in Masuria, Poland — a Teutonic Order commandery turned castle hotel with a spa. From approx. €125/night.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In the town of Ryn in the Masurian Lake District, next to Lake Ołów; the castle stands by the town's main square.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €125/night for a 16 m² Economy Double with a courtyard view; an 18 m² Standard Double with a city view also starts around €126. Breakfast is not included at this rate — it's available for approx. €16 extra, or as part of a pricier breakfast-included room.

**On-site:** The hotel's restaurant Refektarz serves dishes inspired by Teutonic Knights' cuisine, and there is a castle spa; the hotel also runs knightly feasts and courtyard events.

**Good to know:** Ryn is a conference and leisure hotel as well as a castle, so weekends can be busy with events. Most of the building is a later reconstruction after the fires of 1657 and 1881, not untouched 14th-century fabric.

**Combine with:** The Masurian lakes around Giżycko; [Boyen Fortress](/castles/poland/boyen-fortress) is a short drive away.
